comments.comment: I firmly believe in this message. This is an incredible important battle in our culture
Yes ❤️

If you stand for protecting babies in the womb then don't forget to also help and protect them outside of the womb. There are many women who are not prepared or able to care for babies. Babies and children suffer a lot of trauma when that is the case. If we fight for them to be born we should also be fighting for them to live good healthy lives by giving the women resources for therapy and classes and also by serving them and helping where we can. The church also supports abortions in certain cases.

This article doesn’t offer a “candid” look at the issue but instead tries to dismiss real concerns that exist and offers weak arguments as to why they should be dismissed. The author makes a wild assumption about the real reasons Latter-Day Saints might oppose certain legislation or “shy away” from the issue. It’s offensive to suggest that the real reason members shy away from the issue is because pro-life is “gauche”. I don’t believe members of the church view the sanctity of life as gauche. The issue of pro-life/pro-choice is incredibly nuanced. I stand with the church on the issue and will continue to support women, children (born and unborn) through my support of leaders who offer solutions rather than judgments and through legislation that is thoughtful and meaningful and remains in accordance with what the church has stated in regards to the issue. If we really want to promote the pro-life movement then we need to do a lot more work supporting women and children and healthcare.

This article grossly misrepresents the abortion law landscape across the US. 41 states have abortion bans, and 13 of those have virtually no exceptions. Wyoming just passed a law banning abortion even in cases of rape or incest. How about we start protecting women better and holding men accountable for creating unwanted pregnancies in the first place?
I will stand up for choice and for healthcare. Abortion is healthcare. Women and their healthcare providers should be able to make informed choices safely and without threat of legal punishment.
By the way. There is never a mention of the responsibility of the men in this discussion. It always falls on the women.

Let’s remember these folks are the same people who won’t fund health care for all decent housing free school lunches public education and that doesn’t mention dental care and a host of other social programs that care for the born. Upon the child’s first breath they and their infants are on their own I would not have an abortion I don’t think they are great. I don’t get to enforce my beliefs on others.
Yes! I want to be more involved! I love learning from @latterdaysaintsforlife too. They do amazing work!
I prefer freedom, and I don't want to live in a theocracy. The US is a secular society, and I don't want anyone's religious beliefs, even my own, to be forced upon the entire population

This article doesn’t recognize that women’s healthcare is consistently underfunded and underrepresented. I’m pro choice because I am for all the healthcare that female bodies need,including any kind of reproductive healthcare deemed necessary by a woman and her doctor. It is so dangerous to a woman’s body to make laws that limit that healthcare. And I firmly believe that God, who created women’s bodies, want them taken care of as well.

Completely true. Friends of other faiths have largely filled the frontlines (and all the lines) of this fight. We need the Latter-day Saints to step forward. This is perhaps the greatest service we can offer the world: saving the lives of God’s children.
From my experience at the UN, I saw how the Pro-Family movement is being spearheaded by Latter-day Saints. But they still need our help!
Amen! We have good people fighting but we need more!!
So many are supposedly active LDS, and yet vote for candidates that are pro abortion, don’t understand how you can do both!!
The LDS Church is Pro-choice. Read the doctrine.

Some reports claim already expensive cost of having a child have risen 35% since 2023. How can we support legislation that penalizes already financially struggling parent(s) who will incur these prohibitively expensive realities? We are a family supporting church. The family as a whole is central to God’s plan, so why would we encourage policies and practices that leave a measurable negative impact every member of a family negatively if they are suffering financially? The term “unwanted pregnancy” is not the correct term to use. Instead we should call them unsupported pregnancies that can financially ruin families for generations to come. If the church supports pro-life they should consider advocating supporting women with evidence based measures that 1. Financially secure children and women will be supported world-wide. 2 they should help to provide child care expenses after the child is old enough to contribute to the home on their financially. I personal would be happy to support pro-life as soon as social determinants of health are available on a large scale, one by one. Only then will I support women bringing unsupported children to the world. Imagine a woman who is unwed becoming pregnant then having to financially support themselves and the child, with all the stigma this brings. It could ruin her and her family. Start with support focused on the whole family first, then work to improve the circumstances for that child

Abortion laws in many U.S. states restrict access to medically necessary abortions, even in cases of severe complications or risks to the patient’s health. Although most bans contain exceptions to save the life of the pregnant person, these exceptions are often narrowly defined, ambiguous, and create fear of criminal prosecution for doctors. The percentage of medically necessary abortions is roughly 1% to 5% in the U.S. That may be in the “single digits” but that is still lives of women that will be lost due to “radical” abortion laws.

Disagree - let’s work on preventing unwanted pregnancies, supporting women’s ability to choose what’s best for her and her family AND support families. Latter-day Saints do not have a moral obligation to be pro-life.
Using the power of the government to usurp an individual’s bodily autonomy strikes at the heart of the Plan of Salvation. You must have been a fence sitter in the War in Heaven.

When does it become a “child”?
I’m all for pregnancies and babies, but where does it say it’s our job to legislate a woman’s agency? Won’t she ultimately be held accountable and have to answer for her decisions?
Pro life movement is filled with theatrics. It’s off putting we need to do our own thing in defending the unborn.

“As to abortions, we deplore the reported million unborn children who will lose their lives in this country this year. Certainly the women who yield to this ugly sin and the sin which often generated it, and those who assist them, should remember that retribution is sure. It is sure” (President Kimball, Oct. 1974).
